summary: This article explains what fossils are, how they form in layers of rock, how scientists dig them up and date them, and what they tell us about the past, including the Nafud desert in Saudi Arabia.
introduce: Show the three key terms on the board and ask students to rate each one: “I know it,” “I have seen it,” or “It is new.” Tell them to watch for these words in “Fossils: Clues from Long Ago” and use clues around them to understand their meaning.

keyTerms.def: to keep something safe so it lasts a long time
no longer alive anywhere in the world
sand, mud, and tiny bits of rock that settle in layers, often under water

challengeTerms.def: any living thing, such as a plant, animal, or tiny creature
to press something so it takes up less space

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a fossil can tell us more about the past than an old book can? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how rock layers help a paleontologist tell the age of a fossil.
struggling: Pre-teach preserve, extinct, and sediment with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use organism, concealed, and compress in a short paragraph that teaches the class one of the terms with their own example.
